entities.name: Giovanni della Robbia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giovanni della Robbia (1469–1529) was a preeminent Italian Renaissance sculptor, renowned for expanding the family workshop's distinctive glazed terracotta technique across Florence and Tuscany. As the third generation to lead the della Robbia atelier, following his illustrious uncle Andrea and grandfather Luca, Giovanni navigated a period of intense artistic innovation and political upheaval in late 15th and early 16th-century Florence, solidifying the family's artistic legacy while adapting to changing patronage and aesthetic demands. His work, characterized by its vibrant color, durability, and often monumental scale, democratized high-quality religious and decorative art, making it accessible to a broader clientele beyond the Medici court.

Giovanni inherited the della Robbia workshop around 1525, though he had been a primary force in its production for decades prior, contributing significantly to its prolific output. His major commissions include the monumental Lavabo (1497) for the Sacristy of Santa Maria Novella, the Medallions with the Seven Works of Mercy (1514-1525) for the Ospedale di San Paolo in Florence, and numerous altarpieces, friezes, and portrait busts for churches, palaces, and private patrons throughout central Italy. Unlike his predecessors who focused more on subtle modeling, Giovanni often incorporated more complex narrative scenes, naturalistic details, and a wider palette of colors, reflecting the High Renaissance trends of his time while maintaining the workshop's signature luster and relief.
